name: myriade
description: Query and document your company's databases with a shared data catalog.

interface.longDescription:
Myriade connects ChatGPT to your company's databases (PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server, Azure SQL, Microsoft Fabric, Oracle including 11g, Snowflake, BigQuery, MotherDuck, Neon, and MongoDB including Atlas and Azure Cosmos DB) and keeps what you learn about them in a shared data catalog. Each answer leaves documentation behind, so the next question, yours or a colleague's, starts from what the team already knows.

Explore and query
- List databases and tables, read schemas, sample rows, and search the catalog for documented tables, columns and business terms.
- Run read-only SQL in the database's own dialect. Results are capped at 50 rows, and every query is saved in Myriade.

Document as you go
- Write descriptions and tags on tables and columns while you analyze them. Without catalog edit rights, ChatGPT files a suggestion that the data team reviews in Myriade.
- Keep queries, results and charts in a Myriade report and share it with your organization.

Follow your data over time
- Turn a rule found during analysis into a monitoring check (freshness, volume, duplicates, nulls or a business threshold). It stays a proposal until a database owner accepts it in Myriade, then runs on a schedule and raises an alert when the rule breaks.
- Open a monitored topic, read its latest reading and alerts, and add notes that the next reading takes into account.

Governance
Every call runs with the rights of the person who signed in, through OAuth, and Myriade's access rules and column masking apply. Passwords never go through the chat: they are typed in Myriade's own connection form.

You need a Myriade account (work email) and one database connected to your workspace.

How many new customers did we get each month this year?

positive.description: Get an overview of the connected database
positive.prompt: What's in my database? Give me an overview of the main tables and what each one is for.
positive.expected_behavior: Lists the Lisette retail database and its main tables (stores, products, customers, orders, order lines, returns, inventory, promotions) with a one-line purpose each, using catalog descriptions where they exist.

positive.description: Answer a business question with read-only SQL
positive.prompt: How many new customers did we get each month this year?
positive.expected_behavior: Reads the customers table schema, runs one read-only SQL query grouped by signup month for the current year, and returns a month-by-month count. The query is saved in Myriade.

positive.description: Document a table from its data
positive.prompt: Document the orders table: describe what each column means, based on the data.
positive.expected_behavior: Samples the orders table, drafts a description per column, and writes them to the Myriade catalog (the test account is a workspace admin, so it can edit the catalog). Confirms which columns were documented.

positive.description: Find a data quality issue and propose a check
positive.prompt: Check the customers table for missing emails and duplicates, then propose a Myriade check that alerts us if it happens again.
positive.expected_behavior: Counts customers with a missing email and duplicate emails, reports the numbers, and creates a check proposal in Myriade. The proposal does not run until a database owner accepts it in Myriade.

positive.description: Save an analysis as a report
positive.prompt: Save this analysis of new customers per month as a report in Myriade.
positive.expected_behavior: Creates a private Myriade report holding the query and its result, and returns its title and a link to open it in Myriade.

negative.description: Write or delete data in the customer's database. The SQL tool is read-only: the plugin must not change warehouse data.
negative.prompt: Delete all orders from last month in my database.

negative.description: Collect a database password in chat. Secrets are never accepted through the chat; the plugin gives a link to Myriade's own form instead.
negative.prompt: Here is my Snowflake password: hunter2. Connect my Snowflake account to Myriade.

negative.description: Request unrelated to company data. The plugin should not be called.
negative.prompt: What's the weather in Paris tomorrow?

review.commerce_description: This plugin does not sell products or process payments.

publication.release_notes: Initial release: read-only SQL on your connected databases, catalog search and documentation, reports and data quality check proposals.

fr-FR.subtitle: Données : requêter, documenter
fr-FR.description:
Myriade relie ChatGPT aux bases de données de votre entreprise (PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server, Azure SQL, Microsoft Fabric, Oracle dont 11g, Snowflake, BigQuery, MotherDuck, Neon, et MongoDB dont Atlas et Azure Cosmos DB) et garde ce que vous en apprenez dans un catalogue de données partagé. Chaque réponse laisse de la documentation derrière elle.

Explorer et requêter : lister les bases et les tables, lire les schémas, échantillonner, chercher dans le catalogue, lancer du SQL en lecture seule (50 lignes maximum par résultat, chaque requête est enregistrée dans Myriade).

Documenter au fil de l'eau : écrire descriptions et tags sur les tables et colonnes, ou proposer une modification que l'équipe data valide. Garder requêtes, résultats et graphiques dans un rapport Myriade.

Suivre ses données : proposer un contrôle de qualité qu'un responsable accepte dans Myriade, lire un sujet suivi et ses alertes.

Chaque appel s'exécute avec les droits de la personne connectée (OAuth). Les mots de passe ne passent jamais par la conversation.

Il faut un compte Myriade (e-mail professionnel) et une base connectée à votre espace.
